cases.rationale: All required observations are fresh, verified and healthy.
A missing required observation is unknown and never treated as healthy.
Confirmed fixity failure blocks acceptance and produces non-executing recovery proposals.
Integrity can remain healthy while authenticity is unknown without a trusted external anchor.
A support-risk warning schedules reassessment and migration planning, not an immediate integrity failure.
Expired trust-status evidence becomes unknown; historical signature validity is not silently promoted to current trust.
An unverified alert source cannot establish a confirmed calibration failure or a healthy calibration.
Invalid evidence provenance is a blocker and requires independent investigation.
A measured threshold breach proposes inspection and controlled reading without extrapolating lifetime.
The independently assessed number of independent copies is below the declared policy minimum.
Fresh verified fixity evidence explicitly supersedes the prior alert.
A prior active alert cannot clear without a fresh verified remediation observation referencing the alert.
The copy-count metric is below the policy threshold while the observation claims healthy; reject the contradiction.
Future-dated observations are rejected rather than used to claim current health.
An invalidly sourced optional policy signal must still block; non-required must not mean silently ignored.
A later unknown observation cannot downgrade a verified, unresolved fixity alert.
One remediation receipt clears only the alert it names; earlier active alerts stay unresolved.
A remediation receipt cannot clear an alert absent from the evaluated signal history.
A remediation receipt identifier without its independently retrievable content digest is not sufficient.
Only a verified Healthy observation can clear an alert; an Alert cannot itself carry a supersession.
